column1: # RUBRIC TEMPLATE for Nimble Rubric Evaluator. Lines starting with # are instructions and are ignored on import. You can delete them.
# One row per criterion. Level columns go LOWEST first (left) to HIGHEST (right). Write each level header as Label (points), e.g. Developing (1). Use 2 to 10 level columns.
# Type: score (default) or yes/no. For yes/no rows, put what NO looks like in the FIRST level column and what YES looks like in the LAST level column.
# Weight (default 1) sets how much a criterion counts toward the overall %. Question for the model is optional; if blank it is written from the criterion name.
# Describe what you would SEE in the writing at each level, one idea per criterion. Leave a cell blank if a criterion uses fewer levels.
# Save as CSV (UTF-8) and import it in the app under Rubrics > Import & template.

column2: Write a reflective diary entry (200-400 words) about a recent situation at work that did not go as planned. Describe what happened, how you felt, what you learned, and what you will do differently next time.

column4: How clearly and objectively does the learner describe what happened?
column5: The situation is missing, vague or impossible to follow.
column6: The situation is described but key facts (who, what, when, why it mattered) are missing.
column7: A clear account of what happened, who was involved and why it mattered.
column8: A concise, well-structured and objective account with the relevant context and stakes.

column4: How well does the learner examine their own feelings, assumptions and behaviour during the situation?
column5: No mention of own feelings or role; blames others or circumstances only.
column6: Names feelings but does not examine them or their effect on behaviour.
column7: Explains feelings and how they influenced own actions, with some honesty about own role.
column8: Candidly analyses own feelings, assumptions and behaviour, and their impact on others.

column4: How deeply does the learner analyse why things happened and draw transferable learning?
column5: No analysis; restates events without explaining causes or lessons.
column6: Some explanation of causes, but learning is generic (e.g. 'communication is important').
column7: Identifies specific causes and states clear, relevant lessons learned.
column8: Insightful analysis of causes from several perspectives, linked to principles or models, with transferable lessons.

column4: How specific and realistic is the learner's plan for what they will do differently?
column5: No plan or next step is given.
column6: A vague intention such as 'I will try to do better'.
column7: A specific action the learner will take in a similar situation.
column8: Specific, realistic actions with when and how they will be applied and how success will be judged.

column4: Is the entry written in a professional, respectful tone (no insults or confidential personal details about colleagues)?
column5: Contains insults, blame-laden language or confidential personal details about others.
